title: Calculate Age in Years from Birthdate
description: Calculate each customer's **age in years** as of 2026-09-24, classify them into **age brackets** (Under 18, 18-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50+), and count customers per bracket.
solution_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM AGE('2026-09-24'::DATE, birthdate)) < 18 THEN 'Under 18' WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM AGE('2026-09-24'::DATE, birthdate)) < 30 THEN '18-29' WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM AGE('2026-09-24'::DATE, birthdate)) < 40 THEN '30-39' WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM AGE('2026-09-24'::DATE, birthdate)) < 50 THEN '40-49' ELSE '50+' END AS age_bracket, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY age_bracket ORDER BY MIN(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM AGE('2026-09-24'::DATE, birthdate)))
hints: Use AGE('2026-09-24'::DATE, birthdate) to get the interval from birthdate to the reference date, then EXTRACT(YEAR FROM ...) to get whole years.
Use the same CASE expression in GROUP BY, or compute age in a subquery/CTE first to avoid repeating the AGE calculation.
explanation: AGE(reference_date, birthdate) returns an INTERVAL; EXTRACT(YEAR FROM interval) gives whole years elapsed. As of Sep 24, 2026: Jack(2010→16)=Under 18. Eve(1999→27), Carol(2005→20), Grace(2000→26)=18-29. Alice(1995→31), Bob(1988→38)=30-39. Hank(1980→45)=40-49. Dave(1972→54), Frank(1965→61), Ivy(1958→68)=50+. Five age brackets with counts 1, 3, 2, 1, 3.
